talks.description:
Stephen Vintz, Co-CEO, Tenable

AI adoption has been so pervasive it’s created a dangerous illusion of security. Multiple departments in organizations own different aspects of its implementation. The problem? A glaring responsibility gap when it comes to how AI risk is managed and measured. This session outlines how executives and boards must govern this profound cultural and digital evolution, before systemic risk takes hold.

talks.title: A Year(ish) of Countering Malicious Actors' Use of AI: What Have We Learned?
talks.description:
Sherrod DeGrippo, Director, Threat Intelligence Strategy, Microsoft
Cynthia Kaiser, Deputy Assistant Director, FBI
Adam Maruyama, Field CTO for Digital Transformation and AI, Everfox
Lyn Brown, Partner, Wiley Rein LLP

Artificial Intelligence has changed the game when it comes to how cyber adversaries operate, and how defenders respond. This panel will explore lessons learned from the past year of countering malicious cyber actors’ use of AI, challenges and limitations of legal actions involving AI, and what roadblocks might appear going forward as AI, and the actors who use it, continues to evolve.

talks.title: AI and Cybersecurity | Sandra Joyce, Google Cloud & Mohamed Al Kuwaiti, UAE | RSAC 2025
Catch Attackers Before They Strike with AI-powered Threat Intelligence
talks.description: Nation-states and cybercriminals are targeting critical infrastructure with AI-enhanced attacks. Learn from Nadir Izreal, CTO & Co-Founder, Armis, how AI-driven threat intelligence flips the script from reactive to proactive defense—catching attackers in the formulation phase.

talks.title: Countering China's “Typhoon” Threats Targeting US Critical Infrastructure
talks.description:
Marc Raimondi, Chief of Staff, Silverado Policy Accelerator
Brett Leatherman, Deputy Assistant Director, Cyber Operations, Federal Bureau of Investigation
Wendi Whitmore, Senior Vice President, Unit 42, Palo Alto Networks
Tim Maurer, Senior Director, Global Cybersecurity Policy, Microsoft
John Carlin, Partner, Paul Weiss

China’s state-sponsored cyber campaigns—like Volt, Flax, Salt, and Silk Typhoon—are escalating, targeting Western infrastructure. This panel explores how public-private collaboration, informed by cutting-edge industry insight and government coordination, is essential to detect, disrupt, and defend against these evolving threats.

talks.title: Outpace Cyber Threats with Agentic AI + Human Ingenuity | Tomer Weingarten, SentinelOne | RSAC 2025
Podcast: A Conversation with Our Security Strategy & Architecture Program Committee
talks.description:
Speakers:
Abhilasha Bhargav-Spantzel, Partner Security Architect, Microsoft
Kelley Misata, Founder and Chief Trailblazer, Sightline Security & President, Open Information Security Foundation (OISF/Suricata)
Ed Moyle, Partner, SecuirtyCurve
Tatyana Sanchez, Content & Program Coordinator, RSAC
Kacy Zurkus, Director, Content, RSAC

In today’s technological landscape, integrating AI into business operations presents both opportunities and complex security challenges. Our podcast will explore the importance of our Security Strategy and Architecture track, which examines robust security strategies from a diverse set of subject matter experts. We will cover foundational topics including the evolution of defense in depth, advanced threat modeling, adherence to established and evolving security standards and frameworks, and addressing more sophisticated attacks. We’ll also highlight innovative solutions and open-source frameworks shaping security, helping businesses enhance their security posture, comply with regulations, and fully harness emerging technologies to drive growth and efficiency. Additionally, we will explore the trends we have seen this year while reading the submissions. Join us for actionable insights to navigate the complexities of cybersecurity by careful design and implementing effective strategies to safeguard your organization and drive progress.

Listen to more RSAC Podcasts here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library/podcast

talks.title: Podcast: Cybersecurity Insights & Futures: Predicting 2026 with the RSAC Cybersecurity Atlas
talks.description:
Laura Koetzle, Head of Community Research, RSAC
Tatyana Sanchez, Content & Programming Coordinator, RSAC
Kacy Zurkus, Director, Content, RSAC

If we were able to build a tool to synthesize several years of RSAC Call for Submissions, Innovation Sandbox, Exhibitor, and session attendance data, could we predict cybersecurity’s course in 2026? The answer is yes. Join Laura Koetzle, Head of Community Research at RSAC to learn more about the conclusions and predictions -- including ransomware, blockchain, post-quantum security, securing AI agents--published in our first RSAC Cybersecurity Insights & Futures report, which RSAC Members can access at the link below.

talks.title: Protecting AI Infrastructure | Jeetu Patel, Cisco | RSAC 2025
RSAC Innovation Showcase: Agentic Security for the Enterprise
talks.description:
Jenny Brock, Sr. Manager Innovation Programs, RSAC
Swathi Joshi, Deputy CISO, Oracle SaaS Cloud
Aysha Khan, CIO & CISO, Treasure Data
Astha Singhal, Director, Workforce and Infrastructure Security Engineering, Netflix
Chenxi Wang, General Partner, Rain Capital

The RSAC™ Innovation Showcase is a monthly virtual program designed to highlight innovation in cybersecurity. On September 30, we focus on the latest strategies and techniques for engaging agentic AI in your enterprise.

A panel of experts discuss the move from traditional automation to agentic AI systems in security, ways in which these systems can boost productivity & efficiency, risk considerations associated with deploying agentic decision making, and practical security frameworks to help manage these rapidly evolving tools.

The panel then hears from two up and coming companies in the Agentic Security space.

This innovation showcase is hosted in partnership with Rain Capital.

See more RSAC Innovation Showcases here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library/innovation-showcase

talks.title: RSAC Innovation Showcase: AI-Informed Policy Guidance for Cyber Companies
talks.description:
Jenny Brock, Sr. Manager Innovation Programs, RSAC
Katie Gray, Senior Partner, In-Q-Tel
Lucas Nelson, Founding Partner, Lytical Ventures
Matthew Rose, Head of Corporate and Government Affairs, Snowflake

Join us at the RSAC™ Innovation Showcase – a monthly virtual program designed to highlight innovation in cybersecurity. On December 10, we focus on AI-informed policy guidance for cyber companies.

As the threats to cybersecurity and tools to combat those threats are ever evolving, so must the policy and governance of these spaces. Our panel will discuss how companies are thinking about the creation of these policies and how they can protect their businesses.

A panel of experts discuss how AI is shaping policy and governance in the cybersecurity sector, opportunities for startups to leverage policy guidance as a strategic advantage, and staying ahead of best practices and compliance leveraging AI. The panel then hears from two up and coming companies in the cyber risk exposure space.

See more RSAC Innovation Showcases here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library/innovation-showcase

talks.title: RSAC Innovation Showcase: Coding with AI: Can We Trust the Code We Ship?
talks.description:
Moderator:
Jenny Brock, Sr. Manager Innovation Programs, RSAC

Panelists:
Dino Boukouris, Founder & Managing Partner, Altitude Cyber
Tami Bronner, General Partner, Vertex Ventures
Jay Leek, Managing Partner & Co-Founder, SYN Ventures

Can AI truly help us write secure code — or is it just making it easier to ship vulnerabilities faster? Join us as we dive into the challenges of securing AI-generated code and the rise of autonomous testing and remediation. Featuring insights and case studies from AppSec innovators.

A panel of experts discuss how AI is transforming the way developers write and ship code — and where it introduces new classes of vulnerabilities (e.g., insecure code patterns, prompt injection). They also discuss what visibility and validation guardrails are needed before trusting AI-generated output in production, and what successful AI-era AppSec looks like: continuous validation, contextual fixes, and collaboration between dev, sec, and AI systems.

The panel then hears from two up and coming companies in the AppSec AI space.

talks.title: RSAC Innovation Showcase: Leveraging AI in Cybersecurity Workflows
talks.description:
Presenters:
Sid Trivedi, Partner, Foundation Capital
Assaf Keren, CISO, Qualtrics
Jason Lish, Vice President, Chief Information Security Officer, Cisco Systems Inc.

Join us at the RSAC Innovation Showcase – a virtual program designed to highlight innovation in cybersecurity. On February 26, we focus on leveraging AI in cybersecurity workflows.

We are joined by two leading CISOs at cutting-edge software companies who will discuss what role new advances in generative AI are having in improving how cybersecurity teams defend against threat actors.

A few of the topics covered include which security workflows can be most automated through current AI innovations, how security teams are thinking about implementation and budget plans in 2025 and 2026 to leverage GenAI-first security products, and which security workflows are still in need of new AI innovation.

The panel then hears from two up and coming companies leveraging AI to help security professionals reduce their process risk.

See more RSAC Innovation Showcases here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library/innovation-showcase

talks.title: RSAC Innovation Showcase: The New Identity Stack
talks.description:
Moderator:
Jenny Brock, Sr. Manager Innovation Programs, RSAC

Panelists:
Durgaprasad Balakrishnan, Director, Cybersecurity, Visa
Ariel Tseitlin, Partner, Scale Venture Partners
Jonathan Werrett, Head of Security, Semgrep

Join us at the RSAC™ Innovation Showcase – a monthly virtual program designed to highlight innovation in cybersecurity. On August 27, we focus on the ways identity security is shifting from perimeter enforcement to dynamic, contextual access control with a new generation of AI-native solutions.

A panel of experts discuss how AI is operationalizing zero trust at scale, integrating these tools into your identity management stack, and moving your company from reactive policy enforcement to proactive identity intelligence. The panel then hears from two up and coming companies in the identity security space.

See more RSAC Innovation Showcases here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library/innovation-showcase

talks.title: RSAC™ Innovation Showcase: Making a Difference in Application Security
talks.description:
Presenters:
Jenny Brock, Sr. Manager Innovation Programs, RSAC
Mark Kraynak, Partner, Acrew Capital
Jim Manico, Founder, Manicode Security
Elad Menahem, VP of Research, Cato Networks

Join us at the RSAC Innovation Showcase – a virtual program designed to highlight innovation in cybersecurity. On March 27, we focus on application security.

The last mile of protection, actually remediating issues, has always been the hardest in application security. This showcase will focus on innovative approaches to remediation in application security. Experts from Manicode Security and Cato Networks will explore four key topics:

The limitations of traditional application security approaches and the need for solutions that can do more than find issues
How AI and machine learning are transforming vulnerability detection and code remediation
How runtime-based detection and remediation enhance application security
The benefits and challenges of using automated code remediation to address security vulnerabilities

The panel then hears from two up and coming companies in the application security space.

See more RSAC Innovation Showcases here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library/innovation-showcase

talks.title: RSAC™ Innovation Showcase: Mastering OT Cyber Readiness: Strategies & Techniques
talks.description:
Jenny Brock, Sr. Manager Innovation Programs , RSAC
Roya Gordon, Interim Chief Information Security Officer, ENGIE North America
Tansel Ismail, Principal, Energy Impact Partners (EIP)
Tony Surak, Go to Market Partner, DataTribe

Join us at the RSAC Innovation Showcase – a monthly virtual program designed to highlight innovation in cybersecurity. On May 28, we focus on the latest strategies and techniques for OT cyber readiness and protection. A panel of experts will discuss the evolution OT security readiness, the emergence of evidentiary AI in OT security strategies, the use of automation in OT cyber protection, and the benefits and challenges of using automated code remediation to address security vulnerabilities. The panel then hears from two up and coming companies in the OT cybersecurity space.

See more RSAC Innovation Showcases here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library/innovation-showcase

talks.title: RSAC™ Innovation Showcase: New Frontiers in Vulnerability Intel
talks.description:
Presenters:
Grace Cassy, Board Member, Ten Eleven Ventures
Jessica Colvin, Global Head, Cyber Operations, Citi
Chris Corde, Senior Director of Product Management,  Google
Richard Rushing, Chief Information Security Officer, Motorola Mobility

Join us at the RSAC™ Innovation Showcase – a monthly virtual program designed to highlight innovation in cybersecurity. On June 25, 2025, we will focus on the future of vulnerability intelligence and remediation.
A few of the topics covered include the challenges practitioners face, such as prioritization dilemmas, innovative methods including near real-time exploit detection, proactive intelligence, and AI-driven vulnerability prioritization and how to empower organizations to stay ahead of attackers.
The panel then hears from two up and coming companies in the vulnerability intelligence space.
See more RSAC Innovation Showcases here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library#f:contenttype=[innovation%20showcase]

talks.title: Security in the Age of Agentic AI | Vasu Jakkal, Microsoft Security | RSAC 2025
Shaping Cybersecurity: How Regulation Shapes Operational Cyber Defense
talks.description:
Christiane Kirketerp de Viron, Director for Digital Society, Trust & Cybersecurity, DG Connect, European Commission
Tim Maurer, Senior Director, Global Cybersecurity Policy, Microsoft
Ari Schwartz, Managing Director, Cybersecurity Services, Venable LLP
Josephine Wolff, Associate Professor of Cybersecurity Policy, Tufts University, The Fletcher School
Florian Schütz, Director, NCSC - National Cybersecurity Centre

In 2024, elections and growing cyberthreats pushed cybersecurity to the forefront of government priorities. The panel will explore governments’ efforts to strengthen cybersecurity and resilience through regulation, the impact on operational cyber defense, and discuss where greater alignment is possible. Attendees will gain an understanding of the quickly evolving global regulatory landscape.

talks.title: Shaping the Future of AI Security Through Collaboration
talks.description:
Jamil Jaffer, Venture Partner, Paladin Capital Group
Jason Clinton, CISO, Anthropic
Matt Knight, Chief Information Security Officer, OpenAI
Sandra Joyce, VP, Google Threat Intelligence, Google

As the cybersecurity field enters a new AI landscape, collaboration between industry and government is crucial to ensure the advancement of safe and secure AI systems. Sit down with key leaders who are driving AI security to protect the integrity of AI systems and enable the benefits of AI tools for combatting bad actors, safeguarding infrastructure, and bolstering cyber defense.

talks.title: The Future of Tech Policy: Balancing Innovation, Security, and Regulation
talks.description:
Paul Nakasone, Director, Institute of National Security, Vanderbilt University
Chris Krebs, Former Director, Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
Ted Schlein, Chairman & General Partner, General Partner, Ballistic Ventures and Kleiner Perkins

Industry leaders will debate what’s possible when it comes to tech and policy. From cybersecurity regulations to AI policy, deepfakes, and software liability, this session will explore what makes sense, what will stifle innovation, and how to foster collaboration between the public and private sectors to shape the future of tech.

talks.title: Traditional Sessions — RSAC Virtual Seminar: Security Strategy & Architecture
talks.description:
Session 1: Transformational Security Leadership: Strategic Planning, AI Architecture, and More

Modern security leaders must keep up with constant changes to the business, technology, and threat landscape. Transforming your team requires an understanding of how security can protect and enable key business objectives. Come learn how to build a strategic plan, create a business case that resonates with leadership, and secure GenAI architectures in a sustainable way.

Speaker: Frank Kim, Fellow, SANS Institute

Session 2: Security Strategy Framework: Defining Roles, Responsibilities, and Accountability

A typical organization has about 73 security jobs spread across security, technology, and business teams. This session will feature a standard that describes what security jobs exist in an organization and how to set up accountability/responsibility effectively. Will also look at some career antipatterns (common mistakes) for business leaders, security leaders, and security practitioners and provide tips for security practitioners, aspiring leaders, and current leaders.

Speaker: Mark Simos, Lead Cybersecurity Architect, Microsoft

Session 3: Strengthening the Global Financial Sector: Collaborative Approaches to Cybersecurity Threats

Cybersecurity is a team sport.  So why should you be part of the team?  Fostering a corporate culture of collaboration and information sharing is critical – before an incident occurs. Having processes and procedures left of boom matters, especially when trying to make sense of early warnings and consumption of signals that may require proactive measures to shore up cybersecurity defenses. Key topics will include the value proposition of intelligence sharing, pitfalls and pendulums of getting approval to share, trusted communication practices, and strategies for tackling current and emerging threats.

talks.title: Webcast: Breaking the Reactive Cycle: Cybersecurity Through Control Theory and AI
talks.description:
Desire Banse, Security Operations Manager, IdeaCrew

Incidents are leaving defenders trapped in a reactive cycle. This webcast presents a novel framework grounded in cybernetics, control theory, and AI to break free from this loop. Viewing attackers and defenders as feedback systems, and applying AI techniques like active modeling and imitation learning, allows proactive, adaptive strategies that enhance resilience and cybersecurity performance.

See more RSAC Webcasts here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library/webcast

talks.title: Webcast: Building a Secure Al Assistant in a Regulated Industry
talks.description:
Speaker: Kyler Middleton, Sr Principal Software Engineer, Veradigm

Learn how to develop and implement a secure generative Al Slack bot while maintaining strict privacy standards and security requirements. We'll explore the evolution from a basic bot architecture to a fully featured solution, while applying data protection controls that enable secure innovation. We will demonstrate how Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances both functionality and security by constraining responses to approved, segregated knowledge bases. We will also dive into protecting the data in the RAG engines. Through live demos, we'll showcase progressive feature additions and security controls. We will conclude with practical insights from our experience deploying generative Al in healthcare's regulated environment.

Access This and Other RSAC Webcasts with Your Free RSAC Membership. Your RSAC™ Membership also includes AI-powered summaries, mind maps, and slides for Conference presentations, Group Discussions with experts, and more.

talks.title: Webcast: Escalation Paths to Attack Active Directory Certificate Services
talks.description:
Presenter: Derek Melber, Strategic Advisor, Enterprise Identity

The buzz around exploiting ADCS is real, due to there being ten escalations! Also, there are many different combinations of issues that make the exploit possible. Thus, remediation can be complex if attempted manually. However, with free solutions, remediations can be simple and quick. In this webcast, you'll learn how to secure your ADCS installations.

Access this and other RSAC Webcasts with your free RSAC Membership. Your RSAC™ Membership also includes AI-powered summaries, mind maps, and slides for Conference presentations, Group Discussions with experts, and more.

talks.title: Webcast: Leveraging AI for Cybersecurity Workflow Augmentation
talks.description:
Presenter: Gideon Aina, Senior Lead Engineer, AI Security, JPMorgan Chase

This session explores how AI can be leveraged to augment cybersecurity workflows. Attendees will learn about the stages of AI adoption in cybersecurity, practical applications, and a demo of AI-assisted threat modeling. They will leave with actionable steps to begin their journey of integrating AI into their security processes

See more RSAC Webcasts here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library/webcast

talks.title: Webcast: Redefining Security in the Digital Age
talks.description:
Speaker: Jabez Abraham, Director, Product Security Architecture, Dematic

This topic explores how innovative and unconventional approaches by enterprise architects can transform traditional cybersecurity strategies. It examines the impact of forward-thinking architectural practices on evolving security paradigms and how these changes can influence the broader landscape of digital security.

Access this and other RSAC Webcasts with your free RSAC Membership. Your RSAC™ Membership also includes AI-powered summaries, mind maps, and slides for Conference presentations, Group Discussions with experts, and more.

talks.title: Webcast: Surviving the Robot Apocalypse II: LLM Attack and Defend
talks.description:
Presenter: J. Wolfgang Goerlich, CISO, Oakland County, Michigan

Take a long, hard look at generative AI and LLMs. There are defensive and offensive strategies we can employ: prompt social engineering, jailbreaks, and model poisoning. In the near future, in a world potentially dominated by artificial intelligence where machines govern many aspects of life, survival skills may depend on our ability to social engineer those machines. Join this webcast as we explore LLMs and generative AI in the ever-evolving landscape of threats.

See more RSAC Webcasts here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library/webcast

talks.title: Adapting First Order Security Principles to Newer Architectural Trends
talks.description:
Presenter: Char Sample, ICF

Going back to “first principles” can be beneficial particularly, when the landscape changes due to the emergence of cloud, AI, hyperscale, and other trends. This session analyzes architectural trends as they exist in modern designs and takes a “first principles” approach in examining how to approach architecture for modern ecosystems, applications, and environments.

talks.title: Advancing AI Security with Insights from the World’s Largest AI Red Team
talks.description:
Presenter: David Haber, Co-Founder and CEO, Lakera AI

AI security is crucial for current and future digital safety, preventing sensitive data leaks and system compromises. Without robust security mechanisms, confidential information and intellectual property are at risk. This session will share insights from the world’s largest AI red team and discuss what gamifying AI red teaming can teach us about safeguarding AI systems.

talks.title: Agents of Chaos: Hacktivism Spreads Fear, Disinformation, and Propaganda
talks.description:
Presenter: Alexander Leslie, Associate Threat Intelligence Analyst, Recorded Future

Amid wars, disasters, and political instability — hacktivism does little but breed chaos. It has been co-opted by cybercriminals, nation-states, and influence peddlers seeking to advance malign narratives and capitalize on human suffering. This session will address the role of hacktivism in the cyberthreat landscape as one of the primary drivers of malign influence.

talks.title: AI and Democracy
talks.description:
Presenter: Bruce Schneier, Harvard Kennedy School

AI is altering fundamental work of democracy globally: campaigning, voting, writing legislation, enforcing policy, how courts are run and more. Many of the changes will make democracies more responsive to the will of the people, involve citizens ever more deeply in governance, and could make aspects of our society more just, if we begin the conversation now to create secure and trusted AI systems.

talks.title: AI Foundations: Mitigate Risks and Boost SOC Efficiency
talks.description:
Presenters:
Mikiann McIntosh, Compliance Research Engineer, LogRhythm
Sally Vincent, Senior Threat Research Engineer, LogRhythm

In the ever-evolving landscape of cybersecurity, AI-driven automation offers a promising avenue for streamlining SOC efficiency. While the benefits are undeniable, the inherent risks of AI must not be overlooked. Join this session to uncover practical security strategies to navigate the intersection of AI optimization and risk mitigation for a fortified and efficient Security Operations Center.

talks.title: AI in Cyber: Is the Cyber Profession Ready for Its Impact?
talks.description:
Presenter: Clar Rosso, Chief Executive Officer, ISC2

As AI integrates more into the industry, cyber professionals must be aware of the benefits, implications and what others in the industry think of secure adoption and regulation. ISC2 CEO Clar Rosso will share research insights from 1,100 cyber pros. Learn to navigate the transformative impact of AI and enhance your (and your team’s) readiness for the AI challenges and opportunities that lie ahead.

talks.title: AI, the Software Supply Chain, and Other (Not So) Puzzling Pieces
talks.description:
Presenter: Jacob DePriest, VP, Deputy Chief Security Officer, GitHub

As attacks against the software supply chain become more advanced, we must evolve along with them. With the addition of artificial intelligence integrations into the developer toolkit, the old view of supply chain security as just one tool or standard will no longer suffice. This session will examine how AI, with other methods and systems, is magnifying our ability to secure the supply chain.

talks.title: AI-equipped Threat Actors Versus AI-enhanced Cyber Tools: Who Wins?
talks.description:
Presenter: Shiladitya Sircar, BlackBerry

As politicians prepare to face off at the polls, escape their posturing and focus on 2024’s other big confrontation: malicious threat actors leverage AI in a bid to outsmart defenders and their tools. Can the good guys win out with AI-enhanced tools? Learn how to minimize poisoning, carefully curate data, and protect AI tools against adversarial attacks designed to fool the models and poison data.

talks.title: AI: Law, Policy, and Common Sense Suggestions to Stay Out of Trouble
talks.description:
Presenter: Behnam Dayanim, Partner, Global Head, Digital Commerce & Gaming, Orrick Herrington & Sutcliffe LLP

AI is here. Across industries, technologists and businesses are developing new use cases for AI. In so many areas, the law lags the technology, but what are the legal considerations? This session will explore what ethical, legal, and policy considerations must go into AI and what governance structures and benchmarks can help maximize a successful implementation and minimize potential risk.

talks.title: Artificial Intelligence: The Ultimate Double-Edged Sword
talks.description:
Moderator:
Miriam Vogel, Chair of the National AI Advisory Committee (NAIAC) and President & CEO, EqualAI

Panelists:
Fei-Fei Li, Co-Director of Stanford Institute for Human Centered AI, Stanford University
Lisa Monaco, Deputy Attorney General, U.S. Justice Department

AI is still in its infancy. Alongside positive results, dangers have manifest. As new models are introduced, new applications emerge, real-time meltdowns manifest, criminals exploit, and individuals and enterprises scramble to create usage policies that appropriately harness and inform. Join the “Godmother of AI” and DAG Monaco in a riveting keynote discussion on AI’s opportunities and cautions.

talks.title: Building AI Security In: MLSecOps in Practice
talks.description:
Presenter: Diana Kelley, CISO, Protect AI

Are AI systems secure? Not sure how to tell? Starting with an overview of real vs. perceived risks in AI and ML this session will help attendees focus on the most impactful security issues by explaining how MLOps overlaps with DevOps, highlighting areas where the two processes diverge, and providing clear guidance on how and where security can be woven into the ML pipeline.

talks.title: Bye-Bye DIY: Frictionless Security Operations with Google
talks.description:
Presenter: Lorenz Jakober, Head of Product Marketing, Multi-cloud Security Products, Google Cloud, Google

Decades of threat detection, investigation, and response initiatives over-relied on DIY approaches and delivered mostly underwhelming results. This session will introduce Google’s paradigm for modern security operations and demonstrate how recent advancements in applied threat intel, automation, and AI give defenders a chance to flip the script and generate more security outcomes with less effort.

talks.title: CEO Panel: The Entrepreneur Journey to Scale
talks.description:
Moderator:
Robert Ackerman, AllegisCyber Capital

Panelists:
Debbie Gordon, Cloud Range
Robert Lee, Dragos, Inc.
Stuart McClure, Qwiet AI

Join us for an intimate discussion with cybersecurity leaders representing different stages in a company’s journey who will share the secrets to success, entrepreneurial lessons learned, and the challenges of building and scaling a company from early-stage to exit while navigating today's challenging market conditions.

talks.title: Creating an AI Security and Incident Response Team
talks.description:
Presenters:
Lauren McIlvenny, Director, Threat Analysis, Software Engineering Institute Carnegie Mellon University
Gregory Touhill, CERT Director, Software Engineering Institute Carnegie Mellon University

What to do when the AI or ML system is acting funky? How does one know when there is a problem? How can one differentiate between a design defect, data poisoning, or an adversary attack? Who can help? Contact the AISIRT! In this session, the CERT experts will share the process of creating the first AISIRT, the learning insights, and how it can help when a system is causing someone to have a really bad day.

talks.title: Detecting Website Intrusion and Account Compromise with Machine Learning
talks.description:
Presenter: Robin Franklin Guha, Security Engineer, Meta

As more applications become externalized to open environments, the need for a system capable of detecting anomalous activities pre and post-login has become imperative. This session will discuss the approach to detecting misuse or intrusions through machine learning. Covering data, feature engineering, ensemble modeling approach, and integration in a real-time environment.

talks.title: DevSecOps Next: Navigating the Next Era with Industry Titans
talks.description:
Moderator:
Alan Shimel, Techstrong Group

Panelists:
Sid Choudhury, Harness Inc.
Eyal Dyment, JFrog
Basheer Janjua, CloudBees

Explore the future of DevSecOps. Unpack the evolving role of AI, unified platforms, and supply chain security. Gain strategic insights from Techstrong's latest research. #DevSecOpsNext.This session is not just a retrospective but a forward-looking conversation that will equip attendees with knowledge and strategies to navigate the next chapter of secure software development

talks.title: Fight Smarter: Accelerate Your SOC with AI Discovered Attacks
talks.description:
Presenters:
Mike Nichols, Elastic
James Spiteri, Elastic

See how to arm analysts with understanding how to stop attacks rather than triage alerts one-by-one by using generative AI infused with security acumen and environmental context. Live demos and customer use cases will show how AI-driven security analytics help the SOC grasp their most critical events and curate detections, build bespoke remediation plans, and tackle routine tasks.

talks.title: Getting to True Predictive Risk: Will Data Accuracy Thwart AI’s Potential?
talks.description:
Moderator:
Nadya Bartol, Boston Consulting Group

Panelists:
Hyrum Anderson, Robust Intelligence
Edna Conway, EMC ADVISORS | Active Cypher, Attabotics, Critical Start, Cyber Re | Carnegie Endowment for International Peace
Andrea  Little Limbago, PhD, Interos

Dreamt of predictive risk, yet thwarted by inadequate storage, computing, and ML? The jump in LLMs is a step forward but ignores a core part of the AI supply chain--accurate data--hindering progress toward predictive risk. This panel will inspire attendees to seek accurate, data-validated AI/ML models as a core component of AI supply chain security and a critical enabler toward predictive risk.

talks.title: Global Threat Overview
talks.description:
Presenter: Alex Stamos, Chief Trust Officer, SentinelOne

Join this session for an in-depth look at the global threat landscape--from technology and security trends, geopolitical trends and regulatory pressures, to the weaponization of AI. This session will provide insights into how organizations can mitigate risk and ensure resilience in and unpredictable world.

talks.title: Headspace's Privacy Operations Center and Vault
talks.description:
Presenters:
Shobhit Mehta, Security & Compliance Director, Headspace
Puneet Thapliyal, CISO, Hippocratic AI

Headspace and Ginger merged in October 2021 to form Headspace which operates in 170 countries and provides mental healthcare services to more than 100 million members. This session will educate the audience on Headspace's approach to scaling a privacy program and building a Privacy Operations Center. Will take a technical deep-dive into patented Vault architecture.

talks.title: Homeland Security in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
talks.description:
Presenters:
Rumman Chowdhury, United States Science Envoy, Artificial Intelligence, CEO & Co-Founder, Humane Intelligence
Alejandro N. Mayorkas, Secretary, Department of Homeland Security

AI may well be the most consequential technology of our time, with power to innovate and reshape how nations are secured and communities are protected. This fireside chat will explore how the DHS embraces the responsibility to ensure that AI is developed and adopted in a way that realizes its full potential while protecting the public from any harm its irresponsible or adversarial use might cause.

talks.title: How AI Is Changing the Malware Landscape
talks.description:
Presenter: Vicente Diaz, Threat Intelligence Strategist, Google

Last April 2023, VirusTotal implemented several AI engines to assist malware analysis and found AIs interpret malicious code differently than AVs, offering a new angle for malware detection but also showing strong and weak points, like being easily fooled by comments in malicious code. This session dives into insights from analyzing AI-generated malware to different AI-evasion techniques.

talks.title: How Large Language Models Are Reshaping the Cybersecurity Landscape
talks.description:
Presenter: Elie Bursztein, Google & DeepMind AI Cybersecurity Technical and Research Lead, Google DeepMind

From understanding complex instructions, to generating code, to tackling complex problems, Large Languages Models (LLM) exhibit exceptional abilities that are rapidly transforming many aspects of society, including cybersecurity. This talk will draw upon expertise at Google and examine the ways LLMs capabilities are reshaping cybersecurity from both an offensive and defensive standpoint.

talks.title: How Sworn Enemies Found a Truce (Sort of) to Achieve NIST Compliance
talks.description:
Presenters:
Jonall Cobble, Cybersecurity , On the Terrace Tech
Jason Luce, Chief Technology Officer, Paperless Parts

For cyber and engineering teams, it's challenging to achieve alignment on NIST requirements and commit the time and budget to accomplish those goals. It is complicated to effectively translate compliance and security controls to engineering implementation. This session will focus on the journey a startup SaaS company took to gain 3rd party compliance attestation of NIST controls implementation.

talks.title: How to Safely Deploy AI Copilots
talks.description:
Presenter: Brian Vecci, Field CTO, Varonis

Most organizations are evaluating AI productivity tools like Microsoft Copilot, but the biggest reasons it is not yet widely deployed are security and privacy. AI makes it easy to find and use enterprise data, ensuring users don’t have access to what they don’t need is more important than it’s ever been. This session will show an operational plan to deploy Microsoft Copilot quickly while minimizing risk.

talks.title: Innovate Now, Secure Later? Decisions, Decisions…
talks.description:
Presenters:
Mohamad Ali, IBM
Ryan Dougherty, IBM
Srinivas Tummalapenta, IBM Consulting Cybersecurity Services

Businesses are rushing to benefit from AI, but it comes at a detrimental cost when security is an afterthought. Organizations cannot afford to bring unsecured AI models and data into their environments, as attackers will undoubtedly target them for malicious gains. It’s paramount that businesses apply a holistic security framework and embed governance across their AI pipeline and underlying infrastructure.

talks.title: IP Protection and Privacy in LLM: Leveraging Fully Homomorphic Encryption
talks.description:
Presenters:
Benoit Chevallier-Mames, VP of Cloud and Machine Learning, Zama
Jordan Frery, Research Scientist, Zama

Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly utilized in various applications. However, there's a dilemma between safeguarding the model owner's assets and ensuring the user's data privacy. This session introduces a hybrid method that employs Fully Homomorphic Encryption to address both these concerns. Presenting a live demonstration of the approach, highlighting its practicality and efficiency.

talks.title: Keeping Up with the Algorithms: A Journey in Artificial Intelligence
talks.description:
Moderator:
Jon Miller, Halcyon

Panelists:
Jason Clinton, Anthropic
Theresa Payton, Fortalice Solutions LLC
Joseph Szczerba, FBI

What comes before the beginning? As the threat and risk landscape rapidly evolves, AI experts, industry, academia, and the government must race to build a safe and reliable framework for the future. In this session, experts will review how much AI has changed over the last year and discuss what’s on the horizon.

talks.title: Key Management 101: DEKs, KEKs, and Credentials Living Together, Oh My!
talks.description:
Presenter: Karen Reinhardt, Principal Engineer, Cryptographic Services, The Home Depot

Has the ease of Cloud technology resulted in you deploying key management and secrets management tools but not fully understanding all the types of keys managed and how they fit together? This session will cover the different types of keys, their usage, and common management tools, and share some practical advice on how not to run afoul of PCI or give the keys to the kingdom to nefarious agents.

talks.title: Leadership Panel - RSAC 365 Virtual Seminar: Infrastructure Security
talks.description:
Moderator:
Devon Rollins, Vice President and Divisional Information Security Officer for Enterprise Data Machine Learning, Capital One

Panelists:
Rob De Gracia, CTO, Bregal Investments
Thomas Marsland, Board Chairman/CEO, VetSec
Patrick Miller, CEO, Ampere Industrial Security

Leadership Panel: The Journey of a CISO

Traditional network infrastructure has grown more complex as so much of what is IT "native" now bleeds into cybersecurity. What is the impact of digital transformation on legacy systems? Join this panel to hear from IT decision makers who have been at the front of answering that question. We will explore the benefits and challenges of working in collaboration with cloud and security teams and share approaches to overcoming challenges with limited resources, getting tools to work in harmony, visibility into the network, who reports to whom, and more.

talks.title: Leadership Panel — RSAC 365 Virtual Seminar: Securing Cyber-Physical Systems
talks.description:
Moderator: Kasia Hanson, Founder and CEO, KFactor Global LLC

Panelists:
Christian Dameff, Emergency Physician and Clinical Fellow, UCSD
Jeff Gottschalk, Assistant Head of Cybersecurity and Information Sciences Division, MIT Lincoln Laboratory
Megan Samford, VP, CSO US Federal Business & National Security Agreements
Paul Tortora, Director of the Center for Cyber Security Studies and Senior Intelligence Official, US Naval Academy

In 2021, Gartner advised that organizations need to expand their security programs to include cyber physical systems. As we bring 2024 to a close, we see the rampant proliferation of the Internet of Things that are increasingly vulnerable. Are security leaders seeing the direct links between security and the risks of cyber physical systems? How does this link impact the strategic planning process? In addition to identifying the challenges in securing cyber physical systems, this cross-sector panel of cybersecurity leaders will share their unique perspectives on developing and implementing a security strategy that includes cyber physical systems and share insights on developing the team needed to secure critical infrastructure.

talks.title: Leadership Panel: RSAC 365 Virtual Seminar: Intersection of AI & Security
talks.description:
Moderator:
Laura Koetzle, VP, Group Research Director, Forrester Research

Panelists:
Sherron Burgess, CISO, BCD Travel
Arif Hameed, CISO, C&R Software
Royce Markose, CISO, Vistrada
Chris Walcutt, CISO, DirectDefense, Inc.

AI promises to improve productivity and efficiency, but do organizations have realistic expectations and a plan for responsible use? This panel will discuss the realistic expectations and responsible use of AI share ideas to help leaders develop a strategy for implementing AI for cybersecurity while preparing to combat AI-driven cyber threats.

See more of the RSAC Virtual Seminar here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library/virtual%20seminar/hds16-intersection-of-ai-and-security

talks.title: National Security 2030: Social Media and Emerging Cyberthreats
talks.description:
Presenter: Jenny Reich, Fellow and Adjunct Professor, Georgetown Law Center on National Security

Social media has revolutionized everything from what we buy to how we vote. Soon, innovations in AI, AR/VR, and biometrics will meld our digital and physical lives in novel ways. This talk will help cybersecurity professionals navigate this evolving frontier in national security, and will explore how the confluence of new technologies and advanced cyberinfrastructure will shape our digital future.

talks.title: Navigating the AI Frontier: The Role of the CISO in GenAI Governance
talks.description:
Presenters:
James Christiansen, VP CSO, Netskope
James Routh, Board Member, Advisor, Mentor, Faculty Member, Jimmer Advisory Services LLC

Struggling with GenAI control? Join this session to discover the crucial role of CISOs in harmonizing risk management with innovation through proactive AI governance. This presentation will provide an AI Governance Framework and roadmap. Explaining how CISOs seamlessly integrate AI governance into their strategies, safeguarding against risks, ensuring data integrity, and fostering responsible AI practices.

talks.title: Permissions: Centralized or Decentralized? Both!
talks.description:
Presenters:
Sarah Cecchetti, Head of Product, Cedar Policy Language, AWS
Pieter Kasselman, Principal Product Manager, Microsoft

Applications at the edge need to make fast decisions based on local policies. Large organizations need security guardrails that are uniformly enforced. How should a modern business balance these two conflicting needs? The speakers have seen thousands of authorization schemas, and have lots of stories. This session will discuss how permissions structures can be fast, flexible, and globally reliable.

talks.title: Pitfall or Opportunity: GenAI Legal Case Studies Revealing Practical Advice
talks.description:
Moderator:
JJ Jones, Microsoft Corporation

Panelists:
Katherine Forrest, Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP
James Sfekas, Microsoft Corporation
Dondi West, GlaxoSmithKline plc

Using real-world case studies to bring issues to life, this panel of advisors to some of the biggest genAI development and use players around, will address how organizations embracing genAI to drive innovation and fortify their cybersecurity defenses will navigate novel legal challenges and organizational risk and explore pitfalls and alternatives to manage risk in a commercially practical manner.

talks.title: Private Web Search with Tiptoe
talks.description:
Presenters:
Burt Kaliski, Verisign
Alexandra Henzinger, MIT

Web search queries reveal sensitive information about people, leaving a digital trace of their interests and activities. This session presents Tiptoe, a search engine that learns nothing, in a strong, cryptographic sense about what its users are searching for. To provide this privacy guarantee, Tiptoe combines advances in embedding models and modern homomorphic encryption.

talks.title: Regulation on the Horizon: What You Wish Your Lawyer Had Told You About
talks.description:
Moderator:
Beth George, Freshfields Bruckhaus Deringer US LLP

Panelists:
JJ Jones, Microsoft Corporation
Ekaterina Levy, Autodesk, Inc.
Stacey Schesser, Office of the California Attorney General

Governments are passing new regulations faster than VC funds dried up in the Valley. From the SEC’s new rules to California’s proposed cybersecurity audits and the FTC’s novel legal theories on AI to personal liability, there are more opportunities to keep lawyers up at night than ever. Come find out what’s novel, gnarly, and insane—and why to buy your counsel’s next beer.

talks.title: Responsible AI: Adversarial Attacks on LLMs
talks.description:
Presenters:
Saurabh Shintre, LangSafe
Matt Fredrikson, Carnegie Mellon University

Adversarial attacks on LLMs are advancing at a rapid pace, and understanding the challenges is critical to future implementations. Join this session focused on the pivotal research paper Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models to hear a recap on the latest on this ongoing research project and its significant impact on the cybersecurity industry and responsible AI.

talks.title: RSAC 365 Innovation Showcase: Building a Holistic Approach to DevSecOps
talks.description:
Moderator:
Cecilia Marinier, Vice President, Innovation & Scholars, RSA Conference

Panelists:
Anita D’Amico, President, Cotopaxi Consulting LLC
Blake Pennington, Principal, Munich Re Ventures
Tony Surak, Chief Marketing Officer, DataTribe

Join us at the RSA Conference Innovation Showcase – a virtual program designed to highlight innovation in cybersecurity. On June 26, we focus on building a holistic approach to DevSecOps.

Historically, being first to market has been the driving mantra of technology companies trying to win over market share, often at the expense of ensuring security. Government regulation and “Secure by Design” are now forcing tech companies to place some guardrails with innovative startups rising to the challenge by either validating code before production or identifying application vulnerabilities after deployment into customer environments.

Esteemed panelists will discuss historical challenges facing DevSecOps, what shifting left and shifting right means, and where we are in the Secure by Design Journey.

The panel then hears from two up and coming companies in the software lifecycle space.

talks.title: RSAC 365 Innovation Showcase: Identity Security in the World of AI
talks.description:
Presenters:
Jenny Brock, Sr. Manager Innovation Programs, RSA Conference
Aaron Jacobson, Partner, New Enterprise Associates (NEA)
Omar Khawaja, CISO, Client & Faculty, Databricks & Carnegie Mellon University
Allison Miller, Founder & Principal, Cartomancy Labs

Join us at the RSA Conference Innovation Showcase – a virtual program designed to highlight innovation in cybersecurity. On November 25, we focus on Identity Security in the World of AI.

A panel of experts will discuss the latest challenges in identity management and how they affect your organization, the complexities AI introduces to identity security and how to mitigate risks, and tools and techniques for effectively harnessing AI to bolster your security measures.

The panel then hears from two up and coming companies in the identity security and governance space.

Hosted in partnership with New Enterprise Associates (NEA)

talks.title: RSAC 365 Innovation Showcase: The Intersection of AI and Cyber
talks.description:
Meg Anderson, VP-CISO, Principal Financial Group®
Kirsten Davies, 3x CISO
Fredrick Lee, CISO, Reddit
Jason Risch, Partner, Greylock Partners

Join us at the RSA Conference Innovation Showcase – a virtual program designed to highlight innovation in cybersecurity. On September 18, we focus on The Intersection of AI and Cyber.

The intersection of AI and cybersecurity embodies a pivotal frontier in the ongoing battle to protect digital infrastructures from evolving threats. The effective integration of AI into cybersecurity frameworks demands a multidisciplinary approach that blends technological advancements with ethical considerations and uses human expertise to ensure resilient and responsible protection against cyber threats.

Esteemed panelists will discuss:
How are adversaries and defenders deploying in cybersecurity today?
How can companies set policies that harness the power AI offers without potentially exposing the companies to undue risk?
What is the role that cybersecurity professionals play in developing and using AI in cybersecurity to ensure resiliency responsibly?

The panel then hears from two up and coming companies in the AI and Cyber space.

RSAC 365 Innovation Showcase: The Intersection of AI and Cyber—in partnership with Greylock Partners

talks.title: Securing AI Apps with the OWASP Top Ten for Large Language Models
talks.description:
Presenters:
Gavin Klondike, Head of Workshops and Demos, AI Village
Steve Wilson, Chief Product Officer, Exabeam

What are the new risks that generative AI brings to your environment? This session delves into strategies for mitigating risks associated with LLMs, leveraging the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs. Learn to build AI applications with enhanced security, implementing best practices for secure, responsible AI development.

talks.title: Securing Software Supply Chain: Problems, Solutions, and AI/ML Challenges
talks.description:
Presenter: Viswanath Chirravuri, Thales

This session will delve into the critical domain of Software Supply Chain Security, examining real-world recent attacks and the evolving attack surface. Discover the essential frameworks, standards, and references shaping this field, alongside the significance of SBOM. Learn best practices for effective risk mitigation and explore the complex challenges posed by securing the AI/ML supply chain.

talks.title: Shielding the Clouds: Advanced Cyber Defense in Hybrid Environments
talks.description:
Presenter: Craig Connors, CTO, Security Business Group, Cisco Systems, Inc.

Explore an architecture that streamlines security operations in hybrid clouds through unified management of network and workload controls, enhanced by eBPF. Discover how AI shapes consistent security policies across environments, ensuring precision and scalability. Learn about new approaches to effectively enhance security in hybrid cloud ecosystems.

talks.title: Tackling Deepfakes, Wars, and Other Security Threats in the GenAI World
talks.description:
Moderator:
Patrick Huston, FBI AI Task Force

Panelists:
Adam Isles, Chertoff Group
Natalie Pierce, Gunderson Dettmer
Lucy Thomson, Livingston PLLC

Focusing on real-world events that reveal emerging security threats, these cybersecurity leaders will offer insights on how to operate effectively and legally in the age of GenAI. They will delve into cyber trends, C-Suite and board roles, incident response, resilience, and the latest FBI and CISA guidance. They’ll also share initial findings from the new ABA Task Force on Law and AI.

talks.title: The Always-On Purple Team: An Automated CI/CD for Detection Engineering
talks.description:
Presenters:
Stephen Sims, Offensive Operations Curriculum Lead and Fellow, SANS Institute
Erik Van Buggenhout, Director, NVISO & SANS Institute

These speakers will share tips on building the always-on purple team! This session will present an innovative architecture that merges industry-leading SOC technologies, SIEM/XDR, SOAR, BAS, and a pinch of ChatGPT. The result is a detection engineering CI/CD pipeline that can automatically create, test, and deploy detection analytics. The proof is in the pudding: Live demo included!

talks.title: The End of DevSecOps?
talks.description:
Presenter: DJ Schleen, Distinguished Security Architect, Paranoids

If you find yourself with a DevSecOps team and a DevOps team, there's something wrong. Security is simply a quality attribute of existing engineering processes. With the advent of new tools, techniques, and now with Generative AI, we have additional capabilities to simplify communication and reduce toil that we’ve never had before. Find out how to leverage them with an engineering-first approach.

talks.title: The Evolving Role of Emojis in Investigations and Data Security
talks.description:
Presenter: Julie Lewis, Digital Mountain

During this session, we will dive deeper into various aspects of emojis, discuss and demonstrate tools and technologies that can unlock the meaning, intent, and potential digital evidence to enhance investigations, incident response, data security, and provide early indications and warning of potential criminal acts. We will also cover ChatGPT's role in emoji investigations.

talks.title: The Next Application Security Frontier: AI-Ready API Defense
talks.description:
Presenters:
Charles Herrin, F5
Byron McNaught, F5

App modernization efforts have led to the rise of API-based systems and a plethora of interconnections across data center, multicloud, and edge environments. Learn how Generative AI will further API complexity and enhance attack sophistication and democratization—necessitating end-to-end protection from code to runtime and the use of LLM-based security by defenders.

talks.title: The State of Venture Capital in Cybersecurity
talks.description:
Moderator:
Dave DeWalt, NightDragon

Panelists:
Mark Hatfield, Ten Eleven Ventures
Yoav Leitersdorf, YL Ventures
Chenxi Wang, Rain Capital
Nadav Zafrir, Team8

2023 saw a dichotomy of trends converging, with a drop-off in funding tied to the economic downturn alongside a renewed fervor for investment in emerging technologies such as AI amidst ever-rising threats. The result: one of the most unique periods in cyber venture capital history. Leading VCs will discuss how they are approaching this dynamic market and what we may see in 2024 and beyond.

talks.title: Threat Hunting with Python and Pandas
talks.description:
Presenters:
Matt Dulle, Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory
Anthony Talamantes, JHUAPL

This presentation will explore threat hunting in a more iterative, efficient, and scalable approach by exploring the application of data science techniques to cybersecurity data analysis. We will be examining the use of Python, Pandas, and Scikit-Learn to gain additional visibility into threat hunting. We will demonstrate how this approach can work in cyber operations.

talks.title: Traditional Sessions: RSAC 365 Virtual Seminar: Intersection of AI & Security
talks.description:
Session 1: A Checklist for CISOs

This session will cover where to start and discuss the guidance for CISOs published in the OWASP for LLMs CISO Checklist, which includes contributions from a cross-section of security experts.

Speaker:
Sandy Dunn, Serial CISO, Adjunct Professor, Boise State

Session 2: Introducing a Solutions Framework for LLMs, GenAI Security

This session will introduce a new draft framework, published by the project, to help decision makers with categories for security solutions aligned to secure against the LLMs Top 10 Across the LLM application lifecycle.

Speaker:
Scott Clinton, OWASP T10 for LLM Industry Lead

Session 3: Creating and Detecting Machine Learning Model Serialization Attacks

Machine Learning (ML) model hubs are making supply chain attacks possible through ML models. This session will demonstrate how ML models can have malicious code embedded in them during serialization (saving), called Model Serialization Attack (MSA). Attendees will see the step-by-step process to become proficient at both crafting their own MSA and safeguarding against MSA.

Speakers:
Mehrin Kiani, Machine Learning Scientist, Protect AI and Sam Washko, Software Engineer, Protect AI

See more of this RSAC 365 Virtual Seminar here:

talks.title: Use Generative AI to End Your Love/Hate Relationship with DLP
talks.description:
Presenter: Heidi Shey, Principal Analyst, Forrester Research

Design an approach to data security for Generative AI use where DLP is an outcome, and not a single data control. This session will outline how an organization’s use of large language models today will impact the scope of the team's efforts, the AI policy they create and how they align this policy with other enterprise policies, and the different data controls (DLP and others) they can apply.

talks.title: Webcast: Elevating Cloud Forensics: Hypervisor-Level Methods for Evidence Unveiling
talks.description:
Presenter: Prasad Purnaye, Assistant Professor, Dr Vishwanath Karad MIT World Peace University, India

Increasing security incidences in cloud demands vigilant cloud platforms. We propose a novel approach in cloud implementation for detection of potential evidence data using machine learning and AI agent. The proposed AI agent is hypervisor-implementation agnostic and helps to detect and preserve evidence in the form of memory dumps which then can then be analyzed for malwares and other evidences.

See more RSAC Webcasts here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library#sort=%40industrytopiccontentdate%20descending&numberOfResults=25&f:contenttype=[webcast]

talks.title: Webcast: Empower Your Defenses: New Cloud Tools for Securing Vital Applications
talks.description:
Presenter: David Mitchell, Senior Product Manager, IBM Cloud Global Solutions

The cloud offers more than just a bucket for data and applications to be delivered "as a service." Isolated virtual environments, air gap gateways, recovery tools, virtual networking, immutable storage, clean rooms, and new security tools such as scanners and AI are all a part of the next generation of cyber security solutions against advanced threats.

See more RSAC Webcasts here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library#sort=%40industrytopiccontentdate%20descending&numberOfResults=25&f:contenttype=[webcast]

talks.title: Webcast: Hypothetically Speaking—How AI Is Impacting the Education Sector
talks.description:
Moderator:
Doug Levin, Co-Founder and National Director, K12 Security Information eXchange (K12 SIX)

Panelists:
Lisa Einstein, Chief AI Officer, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
Diana Kelley, CISO, Protect AI
Alvin Wang Graylin, Global VP of Corporate Development & Author, HTC & Hachette Book Group

As AI and Generative AI tools become more ubiquitous, they are being implemented in every aspect of our lives, including in K-12 classrooms. With great innovation brings great risk. Will the future of teaching and learning be more or less democratized? What new safety and security risks will generative AI tools introduce? This panel will consider the ways in which the future of K-12 education will be impacted by generative AI. We'll also explore strategies developers can implement to safely deploy emerging technologies, considerations for equitable and fair access to reliable tools, and approaches to security awareness training that can help users think more critically about information produced by AI.

See more RSAC Webcasts here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library#sort=%40industrytopiccontentdate%20descending&numberOfResults=25&f:contenttype=[webcast]

talks.title: Webcast: Securing AI Like a Boss
talks.description:
Presenter: Malcolm Harkins, Chief Security & Trust Officer, Hidden Layer

This webcast delves into crucial aspects of AI security, offering practical insights on integrating robust AI/ML security measures and fostering a proactive security culture. It aims to serve as a comprehensive guide for leaders to effectively secure AI and stay ahead of emerging threats.

See more RSAC Webcasts here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library#sort=%40industrytopiccontentdate%20descending&numberOfResults=25&f:contenttype=[webcast]

talks.title: Webcast: Securing Democracy Through Secure Elections
talks.description:
Moderator:
Hugh Thompson, Executive Chairman, RSAC & Program Committee Chair, RSA Conference

Panelists:
Cait Conley, Senior Advisor to the Director, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
Lester Godsey, Chief Information Security Officer, Maricopa County
Jamil Jaffer, Founder and Executive Director, National Security Institute
Nicole Tisdale, Founder & Principal, Advocacy Blueprints

As we approach the 2024 Presidential election, we know that agents of chaos are actively trying to dismantle public trust in our democratic systems, making it all the more critical for security organizations to build resilient systems while also addressing the impact of disinformation and misinformation campaigns. Join RSAC and a panel of industry leaders who are working to secure democracy by ensuring the integrity and security of our critical infrastructure.

See more RSAC webcasts here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library#sort=%40industrytopiccontentdate%20descending&numberOfResults=25&f:contenttype=[webcast]

talks.title: Webcast: The Magic of Application Security Posture Management and its Future Frontier
talks.description:
Presenter: Vandana Verma Sehgal, Security Relations Leader, Snyk

In this captivating discussion, we embark on a journey into the enchanted realm of ASPM (Application Security Posture Management), discovering its remarkable abilities to fortify our application defenses amidst the ever-shifting digital security landscape. Through proactive risk mitigation, real-time vulnerability management, and the foresight of predictive analytics, ASPM casts a powerful shield around our applications, safeguarding them from the nefarious intentions of cyber adversaries. As we peer into the crystal ball of tomorrow, we envision ASPM soaring to new heights, weaving spells of automation, artificial intelligence, and blockchain into its arsenal, transcending traditional boundaries to protect our digital realm with even greater efficacy. Join us as we unravel the wonders of ASPM and the limitless potential it holds in shaping the future of cybersecurity.

See more RSAC Webcasts here: https://www.rsaconference.com/library#sort=%40industrytopiccontentdate%20descending&numberOfResults=25&f:contenttype=[webcast]

talks.title: What Cloud Has Taught about Securing AI in the Future
talks.description:
Presenter: John Yeoh, Cloud Security Alliance

The rise of GenAI offers unique opportunities and challenges today. As AI integrates into daily life, ensuring its safety and scalability is crucial. This session shares lessons from cloud best practices pivotal for AI technologies. The CSA's AI Safety Initiative promotes responsible AI integration and industry collaboration. This session will present the latest research on cloud security for AI.

talks.title: When Lightning Strikes: The Latest Cyber Law Hot Topics
talks.description:
Moderator:
Ruth Bro, Ruth Hill Bro

Panelists:
Ted Claypoole, Womble Bond Dickinson (US) LLP
Kimberly Peretti, Alston & Bird
Lucy Thomson, Livingston PLLC

Tech-savvy lawyers will conduct a lightning round on critical emerging cyber issues: AI invades our brains; battle strategies against today’s ransomware actors; new groundbreaking Executive Order to protect Americans’ sensitive personal data; promise of GenAI vs. privacy promises; hacking as acts of war under cyber insurance; SEC and other legal duties to protect operational technology; and preparation (Board level and beyond) as the best cyber defense.

talks.title: Your Cybersecurity Budget Is a Horse’s Behind
talks.description:
Presenter: Ira Winkler, CISO, CYE Security

Explore the historical influence of horse-drawn carts on railcar dimensions and how it relates to rigid cybersecurity budgeting. Join this session to learn how to apply machine learning and other mathematical concepts to justify budget allocation, optimize risk, and design effective cybersecurity programs for limited resources.

talks.title: ‘Nurturing’ AI: The Story of How an AI Copilot Was Built
talks.description:
Presenter: Ofir Israel, Check Point Software Technologies

In a rapidly evolving ecosystem, AI sits at the heart of the innovation efforts. This session will unfold the captivating story of the journey in building AI copilots — a process that goes beyond mere programming. We're 'raising' these innovations, akin to nurturing a child to maturity. Join this session as the speakers share their experiences, challenges, and solutions in building AI copilots.

talks.title: .NET 11 in depth: Runtime, libraries, and SDK for the AI era | OD806
talks.description:
.NET 11 delivers a new wave of improvements across the runtime, libraries, and SDK to help developers build modern applications for the AI era. In this session, we’ll take an in-depth look at the key investments in performance, diagnostics, and developer productivity, and how they come together to support intelligent, cloud-connected, and agent-driven apps.

To learn more, please check out these resources:
* https://get.dot.net/11

talks.description:
This session explores how Windows 365 delivers secure, automated cloud experience for development. It covers developer ready images, performance enhancements, and professional grade Cloud PC capabilities. talks.title: Build context-aware agents using GitHub Copilot, Elastic, and Azure AI | DEMSP385
talks.description:
Your AI reviewer has amnesia; it knows your code, but forgets the 2 AM outage from last month. We’ll demo giving Copilot a memory. Using Elastic Agent Builder and Workflows, we build an agent that reviews PRs against production telemetry and incident history. talks.title: Advancing AI and HPC Competency in Higher Education Through Faculty Instructional Enablement
talks.description: NVIDIA’s developer training programs support faculty teaching students and researchers through downloadable teaching kits, a cloud-based GPU-accelerated platform, and technical certification exams. Instructional content spans foundational topics—deep learning, accelerated computing, and data science—and advanced areas including agentic AI, natural language processing, and generative AI. Online courses and instructor-led workshops with project-based assessments help faculty align coursework with certifications and support students in earning recognized qualifications. We highlight ECPI integrating GPU-accelerated AI into student projects, and Lebanese American University using hands-on, faculty-led workshops to advance applied learning and prepare students for real-world AI applications and industry pathways.

talks.title: AI Literacy at Scale: K-to-Career Access That Delivers Real Student Outcomes
talks.description:
AI literacy has moved from a "nice-to-have" to a readiness requirement. The open question is execution: how schools build access that scales, supports educators, and reaches students across different learning paths, geographies, and resources.

This panel brings together education leaders and practitioners shaping that execution from four angles: classroom and school implementation, learning science and workforce-relevant skill-building, platform-level delivery at scale, and institutional systems that connect education to long-term opportunity.

Together, the panel will share practical approaches to expand AI literacy and access without turning schools into pilot sites. You'll leave with a clear view of what to teach, how to equip educators, how to deploy tools responsibly, and how to build pathways that connect early literacy to real-world readiness over time.

talks.title: NVIDIA GTC Automotive Special Address
talks.description: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) are emerging as the first mass-deployed physical AI agents, reshaping mobility and driving new demands in AI, safety, and scalable development. This special address explores the industry’s path to Level 4 autonomy and how NVIDIA is helping accelerate it. With the DRIVE Hyperion architecture, manufacturers (OEMs) and AV developers can build scalable, safety-certified autonomy solutions. NVIDIA will present its cloud-to-car platform—spanning training, simulation, and in-vehicle compute—to support developing and validating next-generation drive-policy models. The session will also touch on how agentic AI is poised to transform AVs end to end, from automating data-driven development and validation to enabling more intelligent, adaptive in-car experiences. Gain insights into L4 software architectures, the DRIVE Hyperion platform, and ecosystem collaboration across OEMs, AV developers, mobility providers, and robotaxi companies.

Learn how your organization can participate in this nationwide effort to bridge the digital divide and accelerate the next era of discovery.

talks.title: Defending against a tidal wave of AI attacks with Lakewatch, the agentic security Lakehouse
talks.description:

Actual, Real, Useful Agents: Bella Liu (Orby) and Eoin Hinchy (Tines)
talks.description:
Bella Liu of Orby and Eoin Hinchy of Tines, both of whom are in the agent business, noted that enterprise customers remain nervous about unsupervised agents running around their IT infrastructure, even as they’re thrilled about the pruductivity potential.

Liu said most Orby agents currently operated with humans in the loop, though the tools do 90% of the work and have “very granular control settings” to prevent rogue behavior.

Hinchy said the key to building trust would be transparency — enabling the customer to see what data is flowing to the agent and what’s coming back. He stressed that agents were essentially an extension of process automation, and would yield huge gains in productivity.

He cited a SaaS company that was able to use an agent to massively decrease the work involved in reviewing code for security problems. Liu gave an example of a healthcare system that was able to dramatically speed up and simplify the on-boarding of new doctors and other providers, which traditionally requires teams of people handling extensive paperwork.

talks.title: AI at the Speed of Thought: Lin Qiao (Fireworks) and Renen Hallak (VAST Data) at CVAI London
talks.description:
Lin Qiao of Fireworks AI said speed and price are going to be crucial differentiators for AI apps, and touted the approach of using open-source LLMs that are customized and closely tied to the application for post-training and inference.

“The continuous loop is the secret sauce,” she said.

Some companies have come up with excellent products but can’t offer them because the compute costs are too high, she said. “Product-market fit and having a viable business are two separate things” in the current moment, she noted, and everyone needs faster performance and lower cost.

Renen Hallak of VAST Data said model-builders and enterprise customers alike need tools to be able to store increasingly massive amounts of both structured and unstructured data, and easily interact with it. GPUs are getting “much hungrier for parallel access,” he said, and the data infrastructure will need to keep up.
